ev.q: Smaller counties were more likely to follow their policies or guidelines than were larger counties (p=0.03).
Among the 66 counties, 58 (88%) screened ≥75% of students in first, third, and sixth grades
Thirty-one counties (47%) used an acceptable electronic data system
Fifty-one of 66 counties (77%) had policies or guidelines for measuring students' weight, height, or BMI percentile.
Nineteen counties (29%) were training ≥90% of their screeners, and 21 (32%) consistently used appropriate equipment
Smaller counties were more likely to use an appropriate stadiometer or weight scale than were larger counties (p < 0.01).
Almost all small counties (36 of 37 counties, 97%) screened ≥75% of students for BMI in first grade
The survey was conducted by e-mailing an electronic survey link to identified coordinators
surveyed school health coordinators in Florida's 67 counties to assess qualities of BMI screening activities

methods_quotes.q: Chi-square test was used to test differences within categories.
A p-value ≤0.05 was considered as statistically significant.
P-value ≤0.05, two-tailed based on chi-square test.
